companies.name: Amazon Music
companies.what_they_did: Amazon Music streams music and audio content to users globally. It integrates music and podcasts into a single destination.
companies.story: Amazon Music evolved to offer both music and podcasts in its flagship application. It serves as a major competitor in the audio streaming market alongside other streaming giants.
reasons: Consolidated music and podcasts into a single application destination
Competed effectively alongside other major streaming platforms
companies.one_line: Offering both music and podcasts within its flagship application.

companies.name: Google Podcasts
companies.what_they_did: Google Podcasts provided a standalone app for streaming podcasts. It allowed users to discover and listen to various podcast shows.
companies.story: Launched in 2018, Google Podcasts gained over 500 million downloads on the Play Store. After a six-year run, Google shut down the standalone app to consolidate its podcast experience into YouTube Music.
reasons: Strategic shift by Google to increase investment in YouTube Music as a single destination
Lower usage of the standalone app compared to YouTube usage
companies.one_line: Shifted podcast investments to consolidate into YouTube Music.

companies.name: Audible
companies.what_they_did: Audible produces and provides spoken-word entertainment and audiobooks. It also produces original and exclusive audio dramas.
companies.story: Audible grew to become the world's largest producer and provider of spoken-word entertainment and audiobooks with millions of members. It continues to expand its offerings with original and exclusive audio dramas.
reasons: Maintained position as the world's largest producer of spoken-word entertainment and audiobooks
Produced original and exclusive audio dramas with strong member retention
companies.one_line: Operating as the world's largest spoken-word entertainment and audiobook provider.

companies.name: Pandora
companies.what_they_did: Pandora offers music and podcast streaming in its flagship application. It acquired Rdio after Rdio went bankrupt.
companies.story: Pandora established itself as a major audio streaming service offering both music and podcasts. It previously acquired assets from bankrupt rival Rdio.
reasons: Offered both music and podcasts in its flagship application
Absorbed market assets from bankrupt competitors like Rdio
companies.one_line: Providing both music and podcasts within its flagship streaming application.

companies.name: Podcastle
companies.what_they_did: Podcastle provides transcription services and audio analytics tools for audio creators. It operates in the audio analytics space alongside other transcription apps.
companies.story: Podcastle grew as an application providing transcription services for podcasts and audio creators. It competes in the audio analytics and transcription space.
reasons: Provided specialized transcription services and audio analytics capabilities
Competed effectively in the growing audio analytics technology space
companies.one_line: Providing transcription services and audio analytics for creators.

companies.name: Tidal
companies.what_they_did: Tidal provides music streaming services with features like lossless audio. It integrates with community-powered platforms like Musixmatch.
companies.story: Tidal built a user base by focusing on music streaming quality, including the introduction of lossless audio. Users frequently switch between streaming platforms to access its features.
reasons: Focused on high-fidelity audio quality features like lossless streaming
Maintained platform integration with major music and lyric syndicators
companies.one_line: Focusing on high-fidelity and lossless audio streaming features.

companies.name: Google Play Music
companies.what_they_did: Google Play Music offered music streaming services to users. It allowed subscribers to stream audio tracks before being succeeded.
companies.story: Google Play Music served music listeners for years before Google initiated plans to shut it down. Users were provided migration options to transition their libraries over to YouTube Music.
reasons: Strategic company shutdown to transition music listeners over to YouTube Music
Consolidation of audio products into a single brand ecosystem
companies.one_line: Shut down by Google to transition users to YouTube Music.

companies.name: Descript
companies.what_they_did: Descript offers audio editing and word-based replacement tools for podcasters. It provides editing solutions for audio production workflows.
companies.story: Descript gained recognition as an audio editing tool used by podcasters to manipulate and replace spoken words. Creators utilize its features during podcast production workflows.
reasons: Provided innovative word-based audio editing replacement capabilities
Integrated smoothly into professional podcast production workflows
companies.one_line: Providing word-based audio editing and replacement tools for creators.

companies.name: Spotify
companies.what_they_did: It operates a major global music and audio streaming service. It offers both music and podcast listening to users.
companies.story: Spotify established itself as a dominant global streaming platform by offering both music and podcasts within its flagship application. It continues to compete globally against other major streaming services.
reasons: Consolidated music and podcasts into a single application destination
Rolled out video podcast support and community features globally
companies.one_line: It maintained its position as a leading global music and podcast streaming service.

companies.name: YouTube Music
companies.what_they_did: It serves as Google's music and podcast streaming platform. It allows users to listen to music and switch between audio and video podcasts.
companies.story: YouTube Music expanded its audio offerings by adding support for podcasts and absorbing listeners from Google Podcasts. It operates as a primary destination for music and podcast fans alike.
reasons: Increased investments in podcast experiences and discovery features
Provided migration tools to absorb users from discontinued services
companies.one_line: It grew by integrating podcast features and absorbing users from Google Podcasts.

companies.name: Apple Podcasts
companies.what_they_did: It provides a dedicated podcast listening application for users. It remains a major standalone platform for podcast content.
companies.story: Apple Podcasts operates as a major player in the podcast space. Unlike other major competitors, it has maintained a separate destination for podcasts rather than consolidating them into its music app.
reasons: Remained one of the major standalone podcast destinations
Maintained broad user access without full music consolidation
companies.one_line: It stayed active as a major standalone platform for podcasts.

companies.name: Apple Music
companies.what_they_did: It offers a music streaming service with extensive track catalogs. It also expanded by launching specialized audio services like Apple Music Classical.
companies.story: Apple Music established itself as a leading global music streaming platform. It continues to compete with other digital streaming platforms through curated music content and specialized apps.
reasons: Expanded its offerings with specialized streaming additions like classical music
Maintained a strong position as a major global streaming platform
companies.one_line: It maintained its strong presence as a global music streaming service.

companies.name: Gaana
companies.what_they_did: It operates as an Indian music streaming service. It competes locally against major global and domestic streaming platforms.
companies.story: Gaana developed as a prominent local music streaming project backed by Times Internet and Tencent. It operates as a key domestic competitor in the Indian streaming market.
reasons: Maintained local market operations backed by strategic media and tech firms
Competed actively against domestic and international streaming apps
companies.one_line: It survived as a key local music streaming competitor in India.

companies.name: JioSaavn
companies.what_they_did: It provides a comprehensive music and audio streaming platform in India. It combines a venture-backed music app with telecom network reach.
companies.story: Saavn raised significant venture funding before being acquired and merged by Reliance Jio to create JioSaavn. The combined entity became a major $1 billion streaming competitor in India.
reasons: Acquired and merged with Reliance's JioMusic service to form a $1 billion entity
Secured strong financial backing and telecom integration for expansion
companies.one_line: It was acquired and merged by Reliance Jio to form a major streaming entity.

companies.name: Resso
companies.what_they_did: It offered music streaming services with social and subscription features. It operated extensively in markets including India.
companies.story: Launched by ByteDance, Resso grew to become a top-grossing music app in India. However, due to local market conditions and government app bans, it was shut down.
reasons: Faced removal from app stores following Indian government orders
Encountered adverse local market conditions leading to complete shutdown
companies.one_line: It shut down operations in India due to government orders and local market conditions.

companies.name: Wynk Music
companies.what_they_did: It functioned as a music streaming application operated by Bharti Airtel. It provided digital music tracks to local users.
companies.story: Wynk Music operated as a notable music streaming app in India created by Bharti Airtel. Eventually, the parent company decided to pull the plug on the service and absorb its employees.
reasons: Parent company Bharti Airtel decided to pull the plug on the streaming app
Absorbed remaining streaming service employees internally
companies.one_line: It was shut down by parent company Bharti Airtel.

companies.name: Night Vale Presents
companies.what_they_did: It operates a network of podcasts featuring surreal and humorous stories. It produces shows set in fictional towns or worlds.
companies.story: Night Vale Presents started as a podcast network featuring surreal and humorous stories set in fictional worlds. It grew to include popular shows like Welcome to Night Vale, Alice Isn't Dead, and The Orbiting Human Circus. It remains active as a podcast network today.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: QCODE
companies.what_they_did: It produces cinematic audio dramas with high-profile actors. It creates scripted audio series for listeners.
companies.story: QCODE started as a studio producing cinematic audio dramas. It grew by collaborating with high-profile actors on popular shows like Blackout and The Left Right Game. It continues to operate as an audio drama studio.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: The Whisperforge
companies.what_they_did: It works as a collective of artists and writers creating diverse audio dramas. It produces immersive fictional audio content.
companies.story: The Whisperforge started as a collective of artists and writers. It grew by producing immersive and diverse audio dramas such as Caravan and StarTripper!!. It is still operating as an audio collective.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: The Wandering
companies.what_they_did: It produces interactive audio dramas with branching narratives. It lets listeners choose their own adventure.
companies.story: The Wandering started as a company producing interactive audio dramas. It grew by offering branching narrative experiences where listeners can influence the story. It continues to produce interactive audio entertainment.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: Gimlet Media
companies.what_they_did: It produces professional podcasts and serialized audio programming. It creates interview series and scripted dramas.
companies.story: Gimlet Media started as an audio podcast venture. It grew its slate of returning and new fall shows, including interview series and scripted dramas. It continues to operate and launch new podcasts.
reasons: Reason not reported
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: Dhingana
companies.what_they_did: It operated an early India-based music streaming service. It provided digital music streaming to users.
companies.story: Dhingana started as an early India-based music streaming pioneer. It faced financial issues and initially shut down its service before being scooped by Rdio in 2014, eventually landing in the startup graveyard when Rdio went bankrupt.
reasons: Acquired by Rdio after experiencing financial issues.
companies.one_line: Acquired by Rdio after facing financial issues.

companies.name: Rdio
companies.what_they_did: It operated a digital music streaming platform. It acquired smaller services like Dhingana.
companies.story: Rdio operated as a music streaming service that acquired Dhingana in 2014. Ultimately, Rdio itself went bankrupt and was sold to Pandora.
reasons: Went bankrupt and was sold to Pandora.
companies.one_line: Went bankrupt and was sold to Pandora.

companies.name: Saavn
companies.what_they_did: It operated an early Indian music streaming service. It merged to form JioSaavn.
companies.story: Saavn started as an early competitor to Dhingana and scaled up after raising $100 million from Tiger Global in 2015. It was acquired by Reliance Jio and merged with JioMusic to create JioSaavn.
reasons: Acquired and merged with Reliance Jio's JioMusic to create JioSaavn.
companies.one_line: Acquired and merged with Reliance Jio to form JioSaavn.

companies.name: Pocket Casts
companies.what_they_did: It operates as a third-party podcast app for listening to shows. It allows users to access podcasts on various devices.
companies.story: Pocket Casts arrived on the scene in 2015 as a third-party podcast app. It helped users discover and listen to podcasts across platforms.
reasons: Maintained open standards and independent podcast directories.
Provided a dedicated app experience for podcast listeners.
companies.one_line: Maintained open standards and provided a dedicated app experience for podcast listeners.

companies.name: Anchor
companies.what_they_did: It provides a platform allowing people to create and publish podcasts directly from an iPhone. It serves as a tool for independent podcasters.
companies.story: Anchor launched in 2016 to let people create and publish a podcast right from their iPhone. Independent podcasters often host their shows there.
reasons: Provided simple mobile creation and publishing tools for independent podcasters.
Served as a hosting platform for independent audio creators.
companies.one_line: Provided simple mobile creation and publishing tools for independent podcasters.

companies.name: Epidemic Sound
companies.what_they_did: It offers subscriptions for unlimited music and sound effects for content creators. It provides direct global licensing for audio tracks.
companies.story: Epidemic Sound offers subscriptions that allow users to use unlimited music and sound effects anywhere online. It sets itself apart with a direct license model covering all rights globally.
reasons: Offered a direct license model with all rights included globally.
Provided unlimited music and sound effects for content creators across platforms.
companies.one_line: Offered a direct license model with all rights included globally.

companies.name: Kadhai Osai
companies.what_they_did: It produces and narrates Tamil audiobooks and stories. It features books narrated by Tamil audiobook narrator Deepika Arun.
companies.story: Kadhai Osai features books by favourite authors narrated as Tamil audiobooks by Deepika Arun. It operates within the Tamil audio stories and podcast space.
reasons: Provided dedicated Tamil audiobook content narrated by leading artists.
Connected Tamil listeners with regional literature and stories.
companies.one_line: Provided dedicated Tamil audiobook content narrated by leading artists.

companies.name: Hoopr
companies.what_they_did: It is an online platform offering royalty-free music and sound effects for content creators. It provides musical content for vlogs, films, and ad campaigns.
companies.story: Hoopr was founded in India as an online platform offering royalty-free music for content creators. It grew to secure funding and provide audio tracks for various media productions.
reasons: Offered an array of royalty-free musical content tailored for content creators.
Secured seed funding to scale operations in the Indian market.
companies.one_line: Offered an array of royalty-free musical content tailored for content creators.

companies.name: Podimo
companies.what_they_did: It operates as an audio subscription service providing podcasts and audiobooks. It has raised significant funding to expand its platform.
companies.story: Podimo operates as a subscription service for audio content. It has raised over $204 million in funding to expand its platform and catalog.
reasons: Raised significant venture funding to expand its subscription audio platform.
Offered a curated catalog of podcasts and audiobooks.
companies.one_line: Raised significant venture funding to expand its subscription audio platform.

companies.name: Hungama Digital Media
companies.what_they_did: It produces and distributes digital entertainment content including music and video. It provides applications for streaming music, video, movies, and podcasts.
companies.story: Hungama Digital Media produces and distributes digital entertainment content. It provides users with applications for streaming music, video, movies, and podcasts.
reasons: Provided diverse digital entertainment services including music and podcast streaming.
Established a broad portfolio of content distribution channels.
companies.one_line: Provided diverse digital entertainment services including music and podcast streaming.

companies.name: Kadhai Osai - Tamil Audiobooks
companies.what_they_did: It features audiobooks of favourite authors narrated in Tamil by Deepika Arun. It operates as a dedicated Tamil audiobook podcast channel.
companies.story: Kadhai Osai - Tamil Audiobooks connects Tamil listeners under one channel to listen to books narrated by Deepika Arun. It ranks among top Tamil podcasts.
reasons: Focused entirely on Tamil audiobooks and literature narrated by leading talent.
Engaged regional listeners across multiple podcast directories.
companies.one_line: Focused entirely on Tamil audiobooks and literature narrated by leading talent.

companies.name: Overcast
companies.what_they_did: Overcast is a third-party podcast app that arrived on the scene in 2014. It provides users with a platform to listen to and manage podcasts.
companies.story: Overcast arrived on the scene in 2014 as a third-party podcast app during a period when podcasts were expanding. It continues to operate as a platform for listening to audio content.
reasons: It provides a dedicated third-party listening experience.
It operates within the open podcast and RSS ecosystem.
companies.one_line: Built a popular third-party podcast app on open RSS standards.

companies.name: Sony Music
companies.what_they_did: Sony Music runs a global podcast division offering multi-territory podcast production. Their teams handle creative, sales, marketing, and business development.
companies.story: Sony Music established a global podcast division to handle modern podcast production. The company continues to offer full-service multi-territory audio and podcast services.
reasons: Offers full-service, multi-territory podcast production.
Leverages dynamic creative, sales, and marketing teams.
companies.one_line: Maintains a dedicated global podcast division for modern production.

companies.name: Hubhopper
companies.what_they_did: Hubhopper operates as a regional aggregator app hosting podcasts. It curates and hosts regional lists for listeners.
companies.story: Hubhopper established itself as a regional aggregator app in the audio space. It continues to host podcasts and curate regional lists for users.
reasons: Acts as a regional aggregator app hosting diverse audio content.
Curates regional podcast lists for listeners.
companies.one_line: Serves as a regional podcast aggregator app.

companies.name: Pocket FM
companies.what_they_did: Pocket FM targets mobile-first consumers in price-sensitive markets. It focuses on vernacular content and offline audio capabilities.
companies.story: Pocket FM grew as an audio startup targeting price-sensitive markets with vernacular content. It secured substantial funding, including a $100M Series D round.
reasons: Targets mobile-first consumers in price-sensitive markets.
Focuses on vernacular content and offline capabilities.
companies.one_line: Scaled successfully by targeting mobile-first consumers with vernacular audio.

companies.name: Kuku FM
companies.what_they_did: Kuku FM builds audio platforms targeting mobile-first users in price-sensitive markets. It provides vernacular audio content and offline features.
companies.story: Kuku FM developed an audio platform catering to price-sensitive markets and vernacular listeners. It expanded its operations and raised a $50M Series C round.
reasons: Focuses on vernacular content for mobile-first users.
Provides offline capabilities in price-sensitive markets.
companies.one_line: Captured vernacular audio demand with strong funding support.

companies.name: Video SDK
companies.what_they_did: Video SDK develops infrastructure for audio and video applications. It secured seed funding to support its developer-focused technology.
companies.story: Video SDK entered the audio and video infrastructure space to support modern applications. It secured a $1.2M seed round to fund its growth.
reasons: Builds scalable infrastructure for audio and video applications.
Secured early seed funding to sustain operations.
companies.one_line: Provided technical infrastructure for audio applications.

companies.name: SkillBox
companies.what_they_did: SkillBox is a community platform for artists to collaborate, share, and sell their work. It also allows users to search and book artists for events and festivals.
companies.story: SkillBox was founded in 2016 in Gurugram as a community platform for artists. It has grown to provide collaboration tools, a blog page, event booking, and mobile applications.
reasons: Operates as a multi-functional community and booking platform for artists.
Provides digital tools for artists to share, sell, and monetize work.
companies.one_line: Built a thriving artist community and event booking platform.

companies.name: Radio FM
companies.what_they_did: Radio FM provided audio and radio streaming services to users. The business was later acquired by Auddia.
companies.story: Radio FM operated as a digital radio and audio streaming service. Its business line was acquired by Auddia on February 29, 2024.
reasons: Was bought out through a business acquisition by Auddia.
companies.one_line: Acquired by Auddia.

companies.name: Tencent Music
companies.what_they_did: It operates a music streaming service in China. It is in the process of a public listing.
companies.story: China's Tencent Music is in the process of a listing that could raise $1.2 billion and value it around that $30 billion mark. It operates in the music streaming space alongside global and local streaming rivals.
reasons: It maintains its position through strong market presence and public listing plans in the music streaming sector.
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: Cloud Village
companies.what_they_did: It operates a music streaming service. It planned a Hong Kong IPO.
companies.story: Chinese Internet giant NetEase delayed the $1 billion Hong Kong IPO of its music streaming service Cloud Village due to volatile trading in the country's major tech companies. The public offering was set to launch but was put on hold due to uncertain conditions following a regulatory crackdown.
reasons: It kept operations running while navigating regulatory crackdowns and volatile trading conditions to delay its IPO.
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

risks_handled.how: Delayed its $1 billion Hong Kong IPO due to uncertain conditions following a regulatory crackdown.

companies.name: Audiomatic
companies.what_they_did: It counts as a podcast startup in India. Those at the helm do it as a secondary passion while maintaining day jobs.
companies.story: Podcast startup Audiomatic entered the Indian audio landscape. Those at the helm of podcasting do it as a secondary passion, maintaining day jobs to pay their bills.
reasons: Founders maintained day jobs to pay bills while running the podcast startup as a secondary passion.
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

risks_handled.how: Maintained day jobs to pay bills while running the podcast startup as a secondary passion.

companies.name: Musixmatch
companies.what_they_did: It provides community-powered lyrics and launched a podcast platform driven by AI and community transcription. It uses natural language processing to improve podcast transcription and search.
companies.story: Italy-based company Musixmatch, well known for providing community-powered lyrics to major music streaming platforms, launched a new platform for podcasts combining AI-generated transcription and community-verified editing. It aims to improve podcast transcription, search, discovery, and sharing.
reasons: It leverages its existing experience in training AI models through lyrics and NLP expertise to provide unique audio analysis tools.
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

companies.name: Wondery
companies.what_they_did: It operated as a podcast studio focused on immersive storytelling and narrative shows. It developed IP that could be adapted into TV shows.
companies.story: Wondery was one of the best studios for documentaries, investigations, and immersive storytelling, successfully developing shows like We Crashed, Dr Death, and Dirty John into TV shows. However, Amazon shut down the narrative arm of Wondery and laid off 110 employees amid an audio division restructuring.
reasons: Narrative shows cost a lot and take a long time to make with low return on investment.
Audiences are usually only highly engaged over the initial series run and launch.
Advertisers are less willing to sponsor narrative shows due to unknown reach and limited run.
companies.one_line: Narrative shows cost a lot to make, take a long time to make, and don't often produce a high return on investment.

companies.name: Pantheon Media
companies.what_they_did: It operates a network that features music and sports podcasts. It includes shows like the official Metallica podcast on its roster.
companies.story: Pantheon Media established a network featuring music and sports podcasts. Its co-founders discuss the rights fee structure and fair use grounds to feature popular music in their shows without getting sued.
reasons: It relies on fair use grounds and education commentary to feature popular music in its shows safely.
companies.one_line: Reason not reported

risks_handled.how: Relied on fair use grounds and education commentary to feature popular music without being shut down or sued.

companies.name: Pineapple Street Studios
companies.what_they_did: It operated as a prestige podcast company. Its parent radio station owner filed for bankruptcy.
companies.story: Prestige podcast company Pineapple Street Studios shut down. Its radio station owner, formerly known as Entercom, filed for bankruptcy citing a steep decline in advertising revenue.
reasons: Steep decline in advertising revenue led to the parent company filing for bankruptcy.
companies.one_line: The radio station owner filed for bankruptcy citing a steep decline in advertising revenue.

companies.name: Buzzsprout
companies.what_they_did: It operates as a podcast publishing platform. Its RSS feed meets all the standards for Apple Podcasts.
companies.story: Buzzsprout operates as a podcast publishing platform helping creators publish and distribute podcasts using RSS feeds that meet standard requirements.
reasons: It provides podcast publishing and RSS feed tools that meet industry standards for creators.
companies.one_line: Reason not reported
